EXW.name: Ex Works
EXW.shortDesc: The seller makes the goods available at their premises. The buyer arranges all transport and carries the risk from that point.
EXW.full: Collection of the goods from the seller's premises
EXW.pt: Risk passes the moment the goods are made available at the seller's premises
sl: Making the goods available at the warehouse
bl: Carriage to the port or border
EXW.warn: EXW puts maximum risk on the buyer, including export clearance, which is hard to handle without a presence in the seller's country. In practice FCA is often used instead.

FCA.name: Free Carrier
FCA.shortDesc: The seller delivers the goods to a carrier named by the buyer. Risk passes once the goods are loaded.
FCA.full: Delivery of the goods to a named carrier
FCA.pt: Risk passes once the goods are handed to the buyer's carrier at the agreed place
sl: Loading (if the place is the seller's premises)
FCA.warn: FCA is the recommended replacement for FOB in container transport. Risk passes at the agreed place, before the goods reach the vessel.

FAS.name: Free Alongside Ship
FAS.shortDesc: The seller delivers the goods alongside the vessel at the port of loading. Sea freight only.
FAS.pt: Risk passes once the goods are alongside the vessel at the port of loading
sl: Placing the goods alongside the vessel
FAS.warn: FAS is used for bulk cargo such as grain, ore and coal. It is barely used for containers, where FCA is a better fit.

FOB.name: Free On Board
FOB.shortDesc: The seller delivers the goods on board the vessel. Risk passes once the goods are on board. Sea freight only.
FOB.pt: Risk passes once the goods are loaded on board at the port of loading
FOB.warn: FOB is for sea freight only. For containers FCA is recommended, as it reflects what actually happens at the terminal.

CFR.name: Cost and Freight
CFR.shortDesc: The seller pays the freight to the port of destination, but risk passes once the goods are loaded. Sea freight only.
CFR.full: Cost and freight to the port of destination
CFR.pt: Risk passes once the goods are loaded on board; the seller pays the freight but not the insurance
sl: Paying the freight to the destination port
CFR.warn: The seller pays the freight, but risk passes at loading. The buyer carries the risk for the whole voyage without choosing the carrier.

CIF.name: Cost, Insurance and Freight
CIF.shortDesc: As CFR, and the seller also pays for cargo insurance. Sea freight only.
CIF.full: Cost, insurance and freight to the port of destination
CIF.pt: Risk passes once the goods are loaded on board; the seller pays the freight and minimum insurance
CIF.warn: CIF only requires minimum insurance (clause C). For valuable goods consider CIP, which requires fuller cover (clause A).

CPT.name: Carriage Paid To
CPT.shortDesc: The seller pays carriage to the destination. Risk passes when the goods are handed to the first carrier.
CPT.pt: Risk passes when the goods are handed to the carrier, even though the seller pays the freight
sl: Paying the freight to the destination
bl: Risk from the handover to the carrier
CPT.warn: Under CPT the seller pays for transport, but risk passes earlier, at the handover to the carrier. The buyer carries the risk during transport they do not pay for.

CIP.name: Carriage and Insurance Paid To
CIP.shortDesc: As CPT, and the seller also insures the goods for the whole journey.
CIP.full: Carriage and insurance paid to the destination
CIP.pt: Risk passes when the goods are handed to the carrier; the seller insures the transport for the full value
CIP.warn: CIP requires cover at Institute Cargo Clauses (A) level, the widest protection. That is what separates it from CIF, which only requires clause (C).

DAP.name: Delivered At Place
DAP.shortDesc: The seller delivers the goods ready for unloading at the agreed destination.
DAP.pt: Risk passes once the goods reach the agreed destination, before unloading
DAP.warn: The seller is not responsible for unloading. If the delivery place does not let the seller unload, consider DPU.

DPU.name: Delivered at Place Unloaded
DPU.shortDesc: As DAP, but the seller is also responsible for unloading the goods at the destination.
DPU.full: Delivery unloaded at the agreed place
DPU.pt: Risk passes only after the goods are unloaded at the destination
DPU.warn: DPU is the only Incoterm where the seller is responsible for unloading. It was called DAT before and was renamed in Incoterms 2020.

DDP.name: Delivered Duty Paid
DDP.shortDesc: The seller delivers the goods cleared for import, with duty and taxes paid, ready for unloading.
DDP.pt: Risk passes only once the goods reach the destination with duty and taxes paid
bl: Taking delivery of the goods at the destination
DDP.warn: DDP requires a VAT and EORI number in the country of import. It is awkward for non-EU sellers and not advisable without knowing the local rules.
